idea: How to prevent bad smells from drains
title: Maintaining the P-Trap Water Seal to Block Sewer Odors
description: When a drain starts emitting foul sewer smells, the most common culprit isn't organic build-up—it's a dry P-trap. The curved pipe section beneath sinks, showers, and floor drains holds a standing water barrier known as the trap seal. This liquid barrier physically blocks sewer gas from traveling up the drainage system into your living space. If a fixture remains unused for extended periods, dry air evaporates this water barrier, leaving an open path for odor. Running fresh water down rarely used drains for 15 seconds replenishes the trap seal and immediately stops sewer gas infiltration.

visual_story: The visual uses a clear educational cutaway of a P-trap to show the standing water barrier at the bottom of the curve. Viewers can immediately see how the trapped water blocks air movement from the waste pipe back up through the drain inlet. This visual reinforces why dry drains smell and demonstrates the physical barrier concept without relying on abstract diagrams.

on_image_text.hook: Why Unused Drains Start to Smell
on_image_text.explanation: The standing water barrier in the P-trap evaporates, opening a direct path for sewer gas.
on_image_text.takeaway: Run water down rarely used drains weekly to keep the liquid trap seal filled.
